title: The residue test on the pro-étale site
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an integer
$n\geq1$ and $A=A_{E,n}$, put $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$, let $T$ be a
scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let
$K\in D^b_c(T_{\Proet},A)$ be a bounded constructible complex of
$A$-modules on the small pro-étale site in the intrinsic sense of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. For integers $a\leq b$, use Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] and derived tensor as in [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Then $K$ has finite
Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ if and
only if the derived tensor product $K\otimes_A^L\kappa_T$ with the
constant sheaf $\kappa_T$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$.

proof.text: If $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, substitute the degree-zero $A_T$-module $\kappa_T$ for $M$ in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. This gives the required vanishing of $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_A^L\kappa_T)$ outside the interval.

For the converse choose a representing complex for $K$ and a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with every $P^q$ flat, using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the ringed site $(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_T)$. By [def-weil-derived-tensor], for every module sheaf $M$ the complex $P\otimes_{A_T}M$ represents $K\otimes_A^LM$. Set $C=P\otimes_{A_T}\kappa_T$. The hypothesis is $\mathcal H^r(C)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$. Neither $P$ nor $C$ is assumed bounded.

Let $N$ be any sheaf of $\kappa_T$-modules. Compute tensors over the constant presheaf $U\mapsto\kappa$, before sheafification: [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] identifies the sheafification of $U\mapsto C^q(U)\otimes_\kappa N(U)$ with $C^q\otimes_{\kappa_T}N$. For each $U$, tensoring vector spaces with $N(U)$ preserves exactness: split a vector-space sequence by lifting a basis of its quotient, so after tensoring it is still a direct-sum sequence. For the section complex, put $Z^r=\ker d^r$ and $B^r=\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}$. Exactness of tensor applied to $0\to Z^r\to C^r(U)\to B^{r+1}\to0$ and $0\to B^r\to Z^r\to H^r(C(U))\to0$ identifies the cycles after tensor with $Z^r\otimes_\kappa N(U)$ and the boundaries with $B^r\otimes_\kappa N(U)$. Hence the canonical map $[z]\otimes y\mapsto[z\otimes y]$, which commutes with restrictions independently of the chosen splittings, gives
$$H^r(C(U)\otimes_\kappa N(U))=H^r(C(U))\otimes_\kappa N(U).$$
By [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], sheafification commutes with cohomology. Sheafify the preceding identity and apply the tensor-sheafification comparison once more to obtain
$$\mathcal H^r(C\otimes_{\kappa_T}N)\cong\mathcal H^r(C)\otimes_{\kappa_T}N.$$
Thus this is zero outside $[a,b]$. Finally the maps $(x\otimes t)\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes ty$ and $x\otimes y\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes y$ are inverse balanced maps
$$(P\otimes_{A_T}\kappa_T)\otimes_{\kappa_T}N\cong P\otimes_{A_T}N.$$
They commute with restriction and differentials, hence define inverse maps of the sheafified complexes by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Consequently $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_A^LN)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. This uses ordinary tensor on $C$, and does not assert that an arbitrary section ring $\kappa_T(U)$ is a field.

proof.text:
Let $M$ be an arbitrary $A_T$-module sheaf. Define $F_sM=\operatorname{im}(\varpi_E^s:M\to M)$ for $0\leq s\leq n$. Then $F_0M=M$ and $F_nM=0$ since $\varpi_E^n=0$ in $A$. Each quotient $G_s=F_sM/F_{s+1}M$ is killed by $\varpi_E$: locally a section of $F_sM$ is $\varpi_E^s m$, whose product with $\varpi_E$ lies in $F_{s+1}M$. Its $A_T$-action therefore factors through $\kappa_T$, so step 3 applies to $G_s$. For each $0\leq s<n$, tensor $0\to F_{s+1}M\to F_sM\to G_s\to0$ termwise with $P$. Flatness of each $P^q$ means precisely exactness of this tensor functor by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], giving a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], the sequence
$$\mathcal H^r(P\otimes F_{s+1}M)\longrightarrow\mathcal H^r(P\otimes F_sM)\longrightarrow\mathcal H^r(P\otimes G_s)$$
is exact. Descending induction on $s$, starting with $P\otimes F_nM=0$, shows that the middle term vanishes for every $r\notin[a,b]$: its adjacent terms are zero by the induction hypothesis and step 3. At $s=0$, [def-weil-derived-tensor] identifies the result with $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_A^LM)=0$. Since $M$ was arbitrary, [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] gives Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$.
